manifest.title: Savitch's Theorem

inputs.abstract: Savitch's theorem states that nondeterministic space $s(n)$ can be simulated in deterministic space $O(s(n)^2)$, for space-constructible $s(n)\geq\log n$. We state this result for the machines of lax-434930 and derive $\mathrm{PSPACE}=\mathrm{NPSPACE}$. The proof separates bounded configurations, recursive reachability, and its machine implementation. The machine implementation and constructibility obligations remain open.

concepts.title: Bounded machine configurations
concepts.description:
A configuration using at most $s$ work cells consists of a control state,
an input-head position, a work-head position, and $s$ work symbols.
Cells beyond this prefix are blank.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434930.SpaceMachines
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi

/-!
---
title: Bounded machine configurations
type: definition
---
A configuration using at most $s$ work cells consists of a control state,
an input-head position, a work-head position, and $s$ work symbols.
Cells beyond this prefix are blank.
-/

namespace Lax307052.BoundedConfigurations

open Lax434930.SpaceMachines

structure Config (M : Machine) (n s : ℕ) where
  state : M.Q
  inputHead : Fin (n + 2)
  workHead : Fin s
  tape : Fin s → M.Γ
  deriving Fintype

def expand {M : Machine} {n s : ℕ} (c : Config M n s) : M.Config :=
  ⟨c.state, c.inputHead.val, c.workHead.val,
    fun i => if h : i < s then c.tape ⟨i, h⟩ else M.blank⟩

end Lax307052.BoundedConfigurations

concepts.title: Runs and configuration reachability
concepts.description:
For a machine whose runs stay within the space bound, bounded configuration
reachability agrees with machine acceptance.

concepts.title: Number of bounded configurations
concepts.description:
For input length $n$ and work bound $s$, a machine with state set $Q$
and work alphabet $\Gamma$ has $|Q|(n+2)s|\Gamma|^s$ bounded configurations.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.BoundedConfigurations

/-!
---
title: Number of bounded configurations
type: lemma
---
For input length $n$ and work bound $s$, a machine with state set $Q$
and work alphabet $\Gamma$ has $|Q|(n+2)s|\Gamma|^s$ bounded configurations.
-/

namespace Lax307052.ConfigurationCount

open Lax434930.SpaceMachines BoundedConfigurations

axiom count (M : Machine) (n s : ℕ) :
  Fintype.card (Config M n s) =
    Fintype.card M.Q * (n + 2) * s * Fintype.card M.Γ ^ s

end Lax307052.ConfigurationCount

statements.signature:
count : ∀ (M : Lax434930.SpaceMachines.Machine) (n s : Nat),
  Eq (Fintype.card (Lax307052.BoundedConfigurations.Config M n s))
    (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (Fintype.card M.Q) (instHAdd.hAdd n 2)) s)
      (instHPow.hPow (Fintype.card M.Γ) s))

concepts.title: The bounded configuration graph
concepts.description:
Vertices are configurations whose work tape has a fixed finite bound.
Edges are machine transitions. Acceptance is reachability from the initial
configuration to a terminal accepting configuration. The search predicate
replaces reachability by the recursive finite graph test.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.BoundedConfigurations
import Lax307052.Reachability
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.EquivFin
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log

/-!
---
title: The bounded configuration graph
type: definition
---
Vertices are configurations whose work tape has a fixed finite bound.
Edges are machine transitions. Acceptance is reachability from the initial
configuration to a terminal accepting configuration. The search predicate
replaces reachability by the recursive finite graph test.
-/

namespace Lax307052.ConfigurationGraph

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.SpaceMachines BoundedConfigurations Reachability

noncomputable def numbering (M : Machine) (n s : ℕ) :
    Config M n s ≃ Fin (Fintype.card (Config M n s)) := Fintype.equivFin _

noncomputable def graph (M : Machine) (w : Word) (s : ℕ) :
    Graph (Fintype.card (Config M w.length s)) := by
  classical
  exact fun a b => decide (M.Step w (expand ((numbering M w.length s).symm a))
    (expand ((numbering M w.length s).symm b)))

def AcceptsBounded (M : Machine) (w : Word) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : Config M w.length s,
    expand a = M.initial ∧ M.Terminal w (expand b) ∧ M.accept b.state = true ∧
    Reachable (graph M w s) (numbering M w.length s a) (numbering M w.length s b)

def SearchAccepts (M : Machine) (w : Word) (s : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : Config M w.length s,
    expand a = M.initial ∧ M.Terminal w (expand b) ∧ M.accept b.state = true ∧
    search (graph M w s) (Nat.clog 2 (Fintype.card (Config M w.length s)))
      (numbering M w.length s a) (numbering M w.length s b) = true

end Lax307052.ConfigurationGraph

concepts.title: Deciding finite reachability
concepts.description:
Recursion depth $\lceil\log_2 N\rceil$ suffices to decide reachability
in a graph with $N$ vertices.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.RecursiveReachability
import Lax307052.ShortPaths
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log

/-!
---
title: Deciding finite reachability
type: lemma
---
Recursion depth $\lceil\log_2 N\rceil$ suffices to decide reachability
in a graph with $N$ vertices.
-/

namespace Lax307052.FiniteReachability

open Reachability

axiom decides_reachability {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a b : Fin N) :
  search G (Nat.clog 2 N) a b = true ↔ Reachable G a b

end Lax307052.FiniteReachability

statements.signature:
decides_reachability : ∀ {N : Nat} (G : Lax307052.Reachability.Graph N) (a b : Fin N),
  Iff (Eq (Lax307052.Reachability.search G (Nat.clog 2 N) a b) Bool.true) (Lax307052.Reachability.Reachable G a b)

concepts.title: Splitting a bounded walk
concepts.description:
A walk of length at most $r+s$ can be split at a vertex into walks of
length at most $r$ and at most $s$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.Reachability

/-!
---
title: Splitting a bounded walk
type: lemma
---
A walk of length at most $r+s$ can be split at a vertex into walks of
length at most $r$ and at most $s$.
-/

namespace Lax307052.PathSplitting

open Reachability

axiom split {α : Type} (R : α → α → Prop) (r s : ℕ) (a b : α) :
  Within R (r + s) a b ↔ ∃ m, Within R r a m ∧ Within R s m b

end Lax307052.PathSplitting

statements.signature:
split : ∀ {α : Type} (R : α → α → Prop) (r s : Nat) (a b : α),
  Iff (Lax307052.Reachability.Within R (instHAdd.hAdd r s) a b)
    (Exists fun m => And (Lax307052.Reachability.Within R r a m) (Lax307052.Reachability.Within R s m b))

concepts.title: Constructing polynomial space bounds
concepts.description:
For every polynomial $p$ with natural coefficients, the positive bound
$p(n)+n+2$ is fully space-constructible.
The machine construction is an open proof obligation.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.SpaceConstructibility

/-!
---
title: Constructing polynomial space bounds
type: lemma
---
For every polynomial $p$ with natural coefficients, the positive bound
$p(n)+n+2$ is fully space-constructible.
The machine construction is an open proof obligation.
-/

namespace Lax307052.PolynomialBounds

open SpaceConstructibility

axiom polynomial_constructible (p : Polynomial ℕ) :
  Constructible (fun n => p.eval n + n + 2)

end Lax307052.PolynomialBounds

polynomial_constructible : ∀ (p : Polynomial Nat),
  Lax307052.SpaceConstructibility.Constructible fun n => instHAdd.hAdd (instHAdd.hAdd (Polynomial.eval n p) n) 2

concepts.title: PSPACE equals NPSPACE
concepts.description:
Deterministic and nondeterministic polynomial space define the same class
of binary languages.
concepts.sourceText:

import Lax434930.PolynomialSpace
import Lax434930.NondeterministicPolynomialSpace

/-!
---
title: PSPACE equals NPSPACE

---

of binary languages.
-/

concepts.title: Bounded reachability
concepts.description:
A directed graph on $N$ vertices is given by its Boolean adjacency matrix.
A walk may repeat vertices. The recursive reachability test divides the
length bound in two and enumerates possible middle vertices.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Mathlib.Logic.Relation

/-!
---
title: Bounded reachability
type: definition
---
A directed graph on $N$ vertices is given by its Boolean adjacency matrix.
A walk may repeat vertices. The recursive reachability test divides the
length bound in two and enumerates possible middle vertices.
-/

namespace Lax307052.Reachability

abbrev Graph (N : ℕ) := Fin N → Fin N → Bool

inductive Walk {α : Type} (R : α → α → Prop) : ℕ → α → α → Prop
  | nil (a : α) : Walk R 0 a a
  | tail {n : ℕ} {a b c : α} : Walk R n a b → R b c → Walk R (n + 1) a c

def Within {α : Type} (R : α → α → Prop) (n : ℕ) (a b : α) : Prop :=
  ∃ k ≤ n, Walk R k a b

def Reachable {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a b : Fin N) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun u v => G u v = true) a b

def search {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) : ℕ → Fin N → Fin N → Bool
  | 0, a, b => decide (a = b) || G a b
  | k + 1, a, b => (List.finRange N).any fun m => search G k a m && search G k m b

end Lax307052.Reachability

concepts.title: Correctness of recursive reachability
concepts.description:
At recursion depth $k$, the search accepts exactly the vertex pairs
joined by a walk of length at most $2^k$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.PathSplitting

/-!
---
title: Correctness of recursive reachability
type: lemma
---
At recursion depth $k$, the search accepts exactly the vertex pairs
joined by a walk of length at most $2^k$.
-/

namespace Lax307052.RecursiveReachability

open Reachability

axiom search_correct {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (k : ℕ) (a b : Fin N) :
  search G k a b = true ↔ Within (fun u v => G u v = true) (2 ^ k) a b

end Lax307052.RecursiveReachability

statements.signature:
search_correct : ∀ {N : Nat} (G : Lax307052.Reachability.Graph N) (k : Nat) (a b : Fin N),
  Iff (Eq (Lax307052.Reachability.search G k a b) Bool.true)
    (Lax307052.Reachability.Within (fun u v => Eq (G u v) Bool.true) (instHPow.hPow 2 k) a b)

concepts.title: Savitch's theorem
concepts.description:
If $s$ is fully space-constructible and at least logarithmic, every
nondeterministic $s(n)$-space decider has a deterministic decider using
$O(s(n)^2)$ space.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.SpaceConstructibility

/-!
---
title: Savitch's theorem
type: theorem
---
If $s$ is fully space-constructible and at least logarithmic, every
nondeterministic $s(n)$-space decider has a deterministic decider using
$O(s(n)^2)$ space.
-/

namespace Lax307052.Savitch

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.SpaceBounds SpaceConstructibility

axiom savitch (s : ℕ → ℕ) (hs : Constructible s)
    (hlog : ∀ n, logSpace n ≤ s n) (A : Language) :
  A ∈ NSPACE s → ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ A ∈ DSPACE (fun n => c * (s n) ^ 2)

end Lax307052.Savitch

statements.signature:
savitch : ∀ (s : Nat → Nat),
  Lax307052.SpaceConstructibility.Constructible s →
    (∀ (n : Nat), instLENat.le (Lax434930.SpaceBounds.logSpace n) (s n)) →
      ∀ (A : Lax434930.PolynomialTime.Language),
        Set.instMembership.mem (Lax434930.SpaceBounds.NSPACE s) A →
          Exists fun c =>
            And (instLTNat.lt 0 c)
              (Set.instMembership.mem (Lax434930.SpaceBounds.DSPACE fun n => instHMul.hMul c (instHPow.hPow (s n) 2)) A)

concepts.title: Correctness of the configuration search
concepts.description:
On space-bounded computations, the recursive configuration search accepts
exactly when the original machine does.
concepts.sourceText:

concepts.title: Space bound for the search machine
concepts.description:
The recursive configuration search can be implemented by a deterministic
machine using $O(s(n)^2)$ work cells. Each recursion frame stores a constant
number of configurations and enumeration counters. This machine construction
is an open proof obligation.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.ConfigurationGraph
import Lax307052.SpaceConstructibility

/-!
---
title: Space bound for the search machine
type: lemma
---
The recursive configuration search can be implemented by a deterministic
machine using $O(s(n)^2)$ work cells. Each recursion frame stores a constant
number of configurations and enumeration counters. This machine construction
is an open proof obligation.
-/

namespace Lax307052.SearchImplementation

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.SpaceMachines Lax434930.SpaceBounds
open ConfigurationGraph SpaceConstructibility

axiom implement (M : Machine) (s : ℕ → ℕ) (hs : Constructible s)
    (hlog : ∀ n, logSpace n ≤ s n) :
  ∃ (c : ℕ) (D : Machine), 0 < c ∧ D.Deterministic ∧
    (∀ w, D.HaltsOn w ∧ (D.Accepts w ↔ SearchAccepts M w (s w.length))) ∧
    ∀ w, D.UsesSpace w (c * (s w.length) ^ 2)

end Lax307052.SearchImplementation

statements.signature:
implement : ∀ (M : Lax434930.SpaceMachines.Machine) (s : Nat → Nat),
  Lax307052.SpaceConstructibility.Constructible s →
    (∀ (n : Nat), instLENat.le (Lax434930.SpaceBounds.logSpace n) (s n)) →
      Exists fun c =>
        Exists fun D =>
          And (instLTNat.lt 0 c)
            (And D.Deterministic
              (And
                (∀ (w : Lax434930.PolynomialTime.Word),
                  And (D.HaltsOn w)
                    (Iff (D.Accepts w) (Lax307052.ConfigurationGraph.SearchAccepts M w (s (List.length w)))))
                (∀ (w : Lax434930.PolynomialTime.Word),
                  D.UsesSpace w (instHMul.hMul c (instHPow.hPow (s (List.length w)) 2)))))

concepts.title: Short paths in a finite graph
concepts.description:
If one vertex reaches another in a graph with $N$ vertices, a walk of
length less than $N$ suffices.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax307052.Reachability

/-!
---
title: Short paths in a finite graph
type: lemma
---
If one vertex reaches another in a graph with $N$ vertices, a walk of
length less than $N$ suffices.
-/

namespace Lax307052.ShortPaths

open Reachability

axiom short_path {N : ℕ} (G : Graph N) (a b : Fin N) :
  Reachable G a b ↔ ∃ k < N, Walk (fun u v => G u v = true) k a b

end Lax307052.ShortPaths

statements.signature:
short_path : ∀ {N : Nat} (G : Lax307052.Reachability.Graph N) (a b : Fin N),
  Iff (Lax307052.Reachability.Reachable G a b)
    (Exists fun k => And (instLTNat.lt k N) (Lax307052.Reachability.Walk (fun u v => Eq (G u v) Bool.true) k a b))

concepts.title: Space-constructible bounds
concepts.description:
A positive bound $s$ is fully space-constructible if a deterministic
machine, on each input of length $n$, halts at work position $s(n)-1$
without leaving the first $s(n)$ work cells. The input tape is read-only.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax434930.SpaceBounds

/-!
---
title: Space-constructible bounds
type: definition
---
A positive bound $s$ is fully space-constructible if a deterministic
machine, on each input of length $n$, halts at work position $s(n)-1$
without leaving the first $s(n)$ work cells. The input tape is read-only.
-/

namespace Lax307052.SpaceConstructibility

open Lax434930.PolynomialTime Lax434930.SpaceMachines

def Constructible (s : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ M : Machine, M.Deterministic ∧ ∀ w : Word,
    M.HaltsOn w ∧ M.UsesSpace w (s w.length) ∧
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (c : M.Config), M.Run w t c ∧ M.Terminal w c ∧
      c.workHead + 1 = s w.length

end Lax307052.SpaceConstructibility

proofs.description: Encode each reachable configuration by its bounded tape prefix and decode each graph edge.
Count the four components of a bounded configuration.
The recursion covers every simple path because $N\leq 2^{\lceil\log_2 N\rceil}$.
Split at the $r$th edge, or at the endpoint when the walk is shorter.
Enlarge the original polynomial bound to $p(n)+n+2$ and square it.
Induction on the recursion depth, using the midpoint decomposition.
Apply the deterministic search machine to a space-bounded nondeterministic decider.
Replace each recursive search by graph reachability and apply the configuration correspondence.
Reachable layers grow strictly until they contain the target; there are only $N$ vertices.
